svg.text: One FastAPI process (modular monolith) + PostgreSQL + Redis. Mock carriers run inside the API but are always called over real HTTP.
every request gets a requestId · JSON camelCase out · expected errors → {"error": …} with HTTP status
includes POST /api/webhooks/{carrier} (the carriers call back here)
create order · idempotent on merchantId + merchantOrderId
fan-out · normalise · Redis cache · select carrier
NDR chat · intent · rules · carrier reattempt
Carrier adapters (carriers/) — translate Zippy ⇄ each carrier's own API
CarrierAdapter.call() (base.py): timeout CARRIER_TIMEOUT_MS · logs · TIMEOUT / HTTP_ERROR / UNREACHABLE
Mock carriers (mock_carriers/) — served at /mock/*, each with a different contract
builds the carrier's own webhook payload → HTTP POST /api/webhooks/{carrier} (back into the routes above)
SQL (psycopg pool): every service reads / writes
End-to-end flow (numbers match the circles above)
UI → POST /api/orders → orders.py → INSERT orders. Same merchantId + merchantOrderId again
POST /api/orders/{id}/rates → rates.py builds the cache key → Redis hit? return.
Miss/refresh → call all 3 adapters in parallel → mock carriers → normalise → save quotes →
cache (300 s, 60 s if partial). One carrier failing or timing out still returns the others.
select-carrier takes the price from the stored quote (client can't change it) → create
shipment books with the chosen carrier through its adapter → tracking number saved, history
Mock Carrier Control → mock carrier sends a webhook in its own format →
shipments.handle_webhook: parse → find shipment → duplicate? → legal transition? → store raw
+ normalized event → update status → NDR creates an NDR case.
Unknown tracking number, illegal status change (e.g. DELIVERED → IN_TRANSIT) or unparseable
payload is stored in webhook_quarantine (HTTP 202/400); the shipment is never changed or
Contact Buyer → buyer message → mock AI extracts intent (date, time) → rules engine decides
ALLOWED / needs approval / unclear → agent reply. The AI never authorises anything.
Rules re-checked → buyer told "submitted" → carrier called (adapter) → only if the carrier
answers ACCEPTED is the buyer told "accepted" and the case RESOLVED. Rejection or timeout
Pages poll GET endpoints every 3–5 s, so webhook and NDR changes appear without reloading.
Rates are fetched once per visit or on Refresh.
Legend: green = business logic · amber = policy · blue = carrier adapters / PostgreSQL · red = mock carriers / Redis · purple dashed = webhook callback into the API
